passages.provision_quote: This state or a city, town, county or political subdivision of this state may not use any of the following voting methods in an election or nomination process for any state, city, town, county or federal office that does any of the following: 1. Allows voters to select or rank, designate or otherwise indicate approval of or preference for more candidates than are eligible to be declared elected for any office. 2. allows ballots cast to be tabulated in any manner that involves the elimination of candidates through multiple rounds of tabulation or the transfer or redistribution of votes between or among candidates.
passages.note: Bill text page prints the operative prohibition but names no voter, so actor and tally fields are null here.
Senate Third Reading roll call records Gowan Y and a divided 16-14 tally; the same page lists him as a co-sponsor.
passages.actor_quote: GONZALES N GOWAN Y HATATHLIE N

rows.reasoning: Gowan is listed as "Gowan (Co-Sponsor)" on HB2552 (2023) and voted "GOWAN Y" on Senate Third Reading, a divided 16-14 vote. The bill is single-subject: its operative section bars any method that "allows ballots cast to be tabulated in any manner that involves the elimination of candidates through multiple rounds of tabulation or the transfer or redistribution of votes between or among candidates." That is a statutory prohibition, matching "Ban ranked-choice voting by law" and excluding the rung that keeps single-choice voting "but stop short of banning it."
